e-5538.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector
e-5538.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the norm, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16+25} \\  & =\sqrt{50} \\  & =5\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-6190.knowledge_point: Factoring a Constant Out of the Norm
e-6190.worked_solution:
Remember that we can factor a constant out of the norm, provided that we take the absolute value of the constant:

$$
\Vert k \mathbf{x} \Vert= \vert k \vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{x} \Vert
$$

Using this fact, we can solve for the norm $\Vert x \Vert$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖-\frac{x}{2}‖ & =5 \\ ‖-\frac{1}{2}x‖ & =5 \\ |-\frac{1}{2}|\cdot ‖x‖ & =5 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot ‖x‖ & =5 \\ ‖x‖ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $\Vert 3 \mathbf{x} \Vert \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖3x‖ & =3\cdot ‖x‖ \\  & =3\cdot 10 \\  & =30\end{aligned}
$$

e-5540.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $\mathbf{x},$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\dfrac{\mathbf{x}}{\|\mathbf{x}\|}.$ Therefore, to normalize $\mathbf{x},$ we first calculate $\|\mathbf{x}\|$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $\mathbf{x}$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{10} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{-8}{10} \\ \frac{6}{10}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector
content.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the norm, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Remember that we can factor a constant out of the norm, provided that we take the absolute value of the constant:

$$
‖kx‖=|k|\cdot ‖x‖
$$

Using this fact, we can solve for the norm $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖2x‖ & =1 \\ |2|\cdot ‖x‖ & =1 \\ ‖x‖ & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $‖-14x‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖-14x‖ & =14\cdot ‖x‖ \\  & =14\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that we can factor a constant out of the norm, provided that we take the absolute value of the constant:

‖kx‖=|k|⋅‖x‖

‖2x‖=1|2|⋅‖x‖=1‖x‖=12

decision.explanation: ‖x‖ = √(4 + 1 + 4 + 9) = 3√2. Dividing each component by 3√2 gives (√2/3, −√2/6, −√2/3, √2/2), which is option e.

after.name: Question 16
after.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+1+4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{3}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?

Normalize the vector x=[2−1−23].

a
[23−23−2622]
b
[1000]
c
[3−6−32]
d
[23−13−231]
e
[23−26−2322]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To normalize a vector x, we have to divide the vector by its norm: x‖x‖. Therefore, to normalize x, we first calculate ‖x‖ as follows:

‖x‖=x12+x22+x32+x42=22+(−1)2+(−2)2+32=4+1+4+9=18=32

Then, we divide x by its length:

x‖x‖=x32=132x=132[2−1−23]=[232−132−232332]=[23−26−2322]

content.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector
content.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+1+4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{-2}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{3}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: ‖x‖ = √(1 + 1 + 0 + 1) = √3. Dividing x by √3 gives (−√3/3, √3/3, 0, √3/3), matching option e.

after.name: Question 17
after.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+0+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector
content.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+0+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find $k$, if $u=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9} \\ \frac{k}{9} \\ -\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}]$ is a unit vector.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{{u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{k}{9})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{(\frac{8}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{81}+\frac{{k}^{2}}{81}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{64}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{74+{k}^{2}}{81}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖u‖=1,$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$

$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{{u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{k}{9})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{(\frac{8}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{81}+\frac{{k}^{2}}{81}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{64}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{74+{k}^{2}}{81}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖u‖=1,$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{74+{k}^{2}}{81}} & =1 \\ \sqrt{74+{k}^{2}} & =9 \\ {(\sqrt{74+{k}^{2}})}^{2} & ={9}^{2} \\ 74+{k}^{2} & =81 \\ {k}^{2} & =7 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Squaring the distance gives (3−k)² + (1−k)² + (2k)² + 2² = 12. This simplifies to 6k²−8k+2 = 0, or (3k−1)(k−1) = 0. Thus k = 1 or 1/3.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -k \\ 2k \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find $k$, if the distance between the vectors is $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the distance between $x$ and $y$ in terms of $k:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}(x,y) & =‖x-y‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{y}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{y}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{y}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{y}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-k)^{2}+(-k-(-1))^{2}+(2k-0)^{2}+(0-(-2))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9-6k+{k}^{2}+{k}^{2}-2k+1+4{k}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14} & =2\sqrt{3} \\ {(\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14})}^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{3})}^{2} \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+14 & =12 \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+2 & =0 \\ 3{k}^{2}-4k+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the quadratic formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4(3)(1)}}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{4}}{6} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 2}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 1}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives $k=1$ and $k=\frac{1}{3}.$

content.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector
content.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -k \\ 2k \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find $k$, if the distance between the vectors is $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the distance between $x$ and $y$ in terms of $k:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}(x,y) & =‖x-y‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{y}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{y}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{y}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{y}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-k)^{2}+(-k-(-1))^{2}+(2k-0)^{2}+(0-(-2))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9-6k+{k}^{2}+{k}^{2}-2k+1+4{k}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $\text{d}(x,y)=2\sqrt{3},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14} & =2\sqrt{3} \\ {(\sqrt{6{k}^{2}-8k+14})}^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{3})}^{2} \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+14 & =12 \\ 6{k}^{2}-8k+2 & =0 \\ 3{k}^{2}-4k+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the quadratic formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4(3)(1)}}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{4}}{6} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 2}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 1}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives $k=1$ and $k=\frac{1}{3}.$

decision.explanation: ‖x‖ = √(1 + 4 + 4 + 16) = 5. Dividing each component by 5 gives (−1/5, 2/5, 2/5, 4/5), matching option a.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector
content.worked_solution:
To normalize a vector $x,$ we have to divide the vector by its norm: $\frac{x}{‖x‖}.$ Therefore, to normalize $x,$ we first calculate $‖x‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide $x$ by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{‖x‖} & =\frac{x}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
